An operation is idempotent when repeating the same request has the same intended effect as making it once. This concerns the operation’s effect, so repeated requests can still create additional log entries.

For example, suppose you send a payment request to charge a customer £20, using the idempotency key `order-123`. You are unsure whether the request completed, so you send the same request again with the same key. A payment API that uses this key to prevent duplicate charges will not create another charge while the stored result remains available. It may still log both requests.

In this hypothetical API, the stored result expires after 24 hours. After that, the same key is treated as new, so repeating the payment request can create another charge. The protection therefore has a time limit.

Idempotency also does not guarantee that a request is authorized. Preventing a duplicate charge and checking whether a request is allowed are separate concerns.
